entities.summary: Hugh Samuel Johnson was a United States Army officer, businessman, speech writer, government official and newspaper columnist. He was a member of the Brain Trust of Franklin D. Roosevelt from 1932 to 1934. He wrote numerous speeches for FDR and helped plan the New Deal. Appointed head of the National Recovery Administration (NRA) in 1933, he was highly energetic in his "blue eagle" campaign to reorganize American business to reduce competition and raise wages and prices. Schlesinger (1958) and Ohl (1985) conclude that he was an excellent organizer, but that he was also domineering, abusive, outspoken, and unable to work harmoniously with his peers.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a key member of FDR's Brain Trust and head of the National Recovery Administration, Johnson played a crucial role in shaping the New Deal, with his 'blue eagle' campaign influencing American business policies. His tenure had significant regional impact on labor laws and economic restructuring.
